registry_disposition.reason: S5 Path-Confinement Closure (owner ticket of 2026-10-21), a bounded closure of the path-confinement finding that the HO-01 lane's independent review raised and deliberately did not repair. The S5 corpus loader in scripts/tools/run-skill-effectiveness-evals.mjs resolved every corpus-declared path LEXICALLY, so a family file that is a symbolic link out of the corpus directory, a family file reached through a symlinked parent directory inside the corpus, and a corpus directory that is itself a symbolic link out of the repository (CLI --corpus) all carried the evaluation out of the corpus the run is supposed to measure. The loader now confines every declared path to the corpus directory in REAL terms and binds every read to a verified file descriptor: the new shared primitive scripts/tools/path-confinement.mjs proves containment twice (C1 lexical, C2 real-path) and binds the read to a verified descriptor (C3 device/inode identity of the descriptor and of the parent directory, opened with O_NOFOLLOW), and requires a regular file (C4). The CLI additionally requires the corpus directory to RESOLVE inside the repository. No CONTRACT_RECORD, PROVENANCE or SUPERSESSION class changes: core/contracts/behavioral-eval.schema.json is untouched, the behavioral-eval validator is untouched, the corpus content is untouched, the BehavioralEvalRecord format is untouched, nothing is superseded, and the evaluation output is digest-neutral (measured: the pristine origin/main tree and this branch produce byte-identical corpus digests, content digests, family digests, and an identical HO-01 comparison record). The runner is a tool surface, not a registered contract. Per the consumer binding in AGENTS.md, NO_CHANGE requires no Registry write; the change registration for this run is projected separately in the Unitera Registry, and the representation in the Unitera Atlas, after the source merge. The TOCTOU residual is documented and not claimed as eliminated: a concurrent writer that replaces the parent directory of the target between the containment check and the open, and that carries a file with the same device and inode identity, is not detectable without openat(2) relative to a trusted directory descriptor, which Node's public API does not expose; the detector for a replaced target IS bound by a test. No independent human approval is claimed: the review of this slice was performed by a tool-driven reviewer on a model different from the one that wrote the slice, with one independent confirmer per finding, and is recorded in the run record.
